payload.title: Basic timeseries manipulation
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook demonstrates basic timeseries manipulation using the Pyleoclim library. It focuses on pre-processing techniques such as slicing, standardizing, and gaussianizing a timeseries. The notebook uses sea-surface temperature data from the NINO3 region to illustrate these methods. Key outputs include plots of the original, standardized, and gaussianized data, as well as summary statistics. The notebook also highlights the use of Seaborn for visual comparison of different data treatments.
goals: Learn to specify a slice of a `Series`
Learn to quickly view summary statistics of a `Series`

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduction to basic timeseries manipulation using Pyleoclim, focusing on pre-processing techniques.
section_blurbs.heading: Basic timeseries manipulation

section_blurbs.blurb: Overview of the notebook's goals and relevant packages, including Pyleoclim, Pandas, and Seaborn.
section_blurbs.heading: Preamble

section_blurbs.blurb: Demonstrates how to slice a timeseries using the `.sel()` method to focus on specific time periods.
section_blurbs.heading: Slicing

section_blurbs.blurb: Shows how to obtain summary statistics of a timeseries using both Pyleoclim and Pandas methods.
section_blurbs.heading: Stats

section_blurbs.blurb: Explains the process of standardizing a timeseries by subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation.
section_blurbs.heading: Standardizing

section_blurbs.blurb: Describes how to map a timeseries to a standard Gaussian distribution using the `.gaussianize()` method.
section_blurbs.heading: Gaussianize

section_blurbs.blurb: Uses Seaborn to visually compare the original, standardized, and gaussianized timeseries data.
section_blurbs.heading: Comparison

inputs: Sea-surface temperature data from the NINO3 region
outputs: Plots of original, standardized, and gaussianized timeseries
